_what: The controls each part draws, by part, in the order they are read (the first declaration of a path keeps its words). Each row is a show-rules `control`: a rule can hide it, or everything under its path, for anyone. The old app reads them in parts/ui/show/show-rules/declared-controls.mjs and the engine in src/local_account/show_rules.rs; each part's part.json stays its manifest.

parts.what: The controls this part draws, each a show-rules `control` (parts/ui/show/show-rules show-of.ts controlShown): a rule can hide any of them, or everything under a path, for anyone. DesktopSidebar draws `<controls>.<capability>` for each capability; a host that draws another frame (the pane tab bar) names its own path.

parts.what: The controls this part draws, each a show-rules `control` (parts/ui/show/show-rules show-of.ts controlShown): every chrome zone is the control `arrangement.<zone>` (read-data/region-chrome.ts zoneControl), so a rule hides it for a person the way a layout's chrome map hides it for a layout. Each part of an empty pane is `arrangement.empty.<part>` (show/EmptyContainer.tsx); hidden, `arrangement.header.tabs.position` keeps the tabs on their default edge.

parts.what: The controls this part draws, each a show-rules `control` (show/show-rules/show-of.ts controlShown). Each row of show/placeable-surface-intent/open-choices.json is also the control `open.<its id>`, and each action a list or record offers is `record.action.<its id>`. The app's own screens declare theirs here too: Your tray (`selection.tray`, src/workspace/tray.json), asking your AI (`ai.*`) and automations (`automations.*`, src/workspace/workflows-screen.tsx).
